description:
In repos/activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts, perform a single-token replacement on one line. The exact substring `detailParam !== 'true'` occurs exactly once in the entire file (verified: 1 match). Replace that one occurrence with `detailParam === 'false'`. Nothing else in the file changes.

The containing statement spans two physical lines (732 and 733) and must NOT be reflowed or rejoined — do not use the whole statement as the match anchor, because a previous attempt failed by collapsing it onto one line and the anchor then matched nothing. Anchor only on the unique substring `detailParam !== 'true'`.

After the edit, line 733 must read exactly:
      fieldsParam === 'summary' || detailParam === 'false';
(six leading spaces, unchanged from the original except for the operator and literal.)

Why: the comment block at lines 718-731 documents the intended contract — "The DEFAULT projection is left WIDE and unchanged - many autonomous consumers (development-vessel resolvers, boredom-vessel) read metadata, composition_chain, failure_mode, and input/output_impulse_shapes off this list response, so narrowing the default would silently break them." But detailParam is c.req.query('detail'), which is undefined when a caller omits the parameter, and undefined !== 'true' evaluates to true, so summaryProjection defaults to true and every unadorned caller silently receives the NARROW projection. The code inverts its own documented default. After this change the wide projection is the default and narrowing stays opt-in via ?fields=summary or ?detail=false, exactly as the comment promises.

Do NOT modify the selectFields ternary near line 887 — its wide branch already correctly lists failure_mode, metadata, output_impulse_shapes and input_impulse_shapes. Do NOT modify the limit clamp near line 736; that is a separate defect and bundling it will cause this patch to be rejected.

Verified live before dispatch: GET /v2/activities/execution-traces?limit=3 returns rows carrying a failure_mode_type scalar and no metadata field, while the identical request with &detail=true returns the same rows carrying full failure_mode and metadata objects. The data is present in the table; only the default projection hides it.
